errors.text_span: The figure illustrates the evolution of key-value (KV) caches in a streaming setting, as described in the paper "SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator." The top plot shows the size of the KV cache, denoted by $ n $, as a function of the number of tokens processed, $ m $, with $ m_0 $ marking a specific point in the sequence. The y-axis represents the cache size, ranging from $ w $ to $ c - a $, and the x-axis spans from 0 to $ m $, with $ m_0 $ indicated as a reference point. The plot depicts a sawtooth pattern, where the cache size increases linearly from $ w $ to $ c - a $, then drops sharply to $ c - a - s $, repeating this cycle. The dashed line at $ c - a - s $ indicates a reduced cache size after compression. The bottom plot shows the size of a running segment, $ \text{Size}_{\text{run}} $, also as a function of $ m $, with the y-axis ranging from $ w + a + s $ to $ c $. The x-axis again spans from 0 to $ m $, with $ m_0 $ marked. This plot also shows a sawtooth pattern, where the size increases from $ w + a + s $ to $ c $, then drops to $ w + a + s $, repeating. The dashed line at $ m_0 $ highlights a specific point in the sequence where the segment size is observed. Both plots demonstrate how the KV cache and segment size evolve over time in a streaming context, with periodic increases and sharp reductions, reflecting the compression and management of data in the model.
